topic: Modal forms in remote apodoses: the reference to Ch. 3
claim: “The most common modal auxiliaries occurring in the apodosis are would, should, could, and might”, and “for other modal forms, see Ch. 3, §§5, 9.8.4”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 3 §5 (p. 139) is “Perfect tense”, and a search of pp. 139–147 for remote, conditional, apodosis and each modal auxiliary finds no discussion of modals in remote apodoses. §9.8.4 is a fitting target: on p. 202 must and ought “occur readily in construction [60ib], if only marginally in [iib]”, where [60ib] is a backshifted report and [60iib] the remote conditional. §2.5 (p. 108), “The auxiliaries considered in turn”, tests each auxiliary for “[L] Can occur in remote apodosis”; p. 109 has %If he had stayed in the army he must surely have become a colonel.
finding: Ch. 3 §5 is the wrong target (high confidence). §2.5 is the likely intended one, but that is an inference (medium confidence).
inference: Does the reference to Ch. 3 lead to the discussion of other modals in remote apodoses?

evidence.passage: §14.2.2, p. 751. “for other modal forms, see Ch. 3, §§5, 9.8.4”
evidence.establishes: Ch. 3 §5 is the wrong target; §2.5 covers the point.
